title: The Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act, 1999

sections.heading: Definition of Geographical Indication
sections.text: 'geographical indication', in relation to goods, means an indication which identifies such goods as agricultural goods, natural goods or manufactured goods as originating, or manufactured in the territory of a country, or a region or locality in that territory, where a given quality, reputation or other characteristic of such goods is essentially attributable to its geographical origin.
sections.relevance: Protects community-origin Ayurvedic herbs and regional botanicals.

sections.section_number: Registered Ayurvedic & Herbal GIs in India
sections.heading: Authoritative Register of Indian Botanical & Medicinal GIs
sections.text:
Key registered GIs include:
- GI-12: Alleppey Green Cardamom (Kerala/Tamil Nadu)
- GI-49: Malabar Pepper (Kerala/Karnataka/Tamil Nadu)
- GI-133: Navara Rice (Kerala - used in Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda)
- GI-186: Coorg Green Cardamom (Karnataka)
- GI-371: Sirsi Supari (Karnataka)
- GI-434: Nilambur Teak (Kerala)
- GI-493: Kashmiri Saffron (Jammu & Kashmir - Crocus sativus)
- GI-610: Dindigul Lock & Kandangi Saree / Erode Turmeric (Tamil Nadu)
- GI-641: Kaji Nemu (Assam - Citrus limon)
- GI-705: Sundarban Honey (West Bengal)
sections.relevance: Authentic regional provenance marketing and GI Authorized User licensing.
